topic: parametric, polar and vector-valued calculus: diagnosing parameter, polar-bound and speed-versus-velocity errors

traps.desc: inverted the quotient and computed dx by dy instead of dy by dx
added the two component velocities instead of taking the magnitude of the velocity vector
integrated over the full turn from zero to two pi instead of over the single petal's bounds, sweeping the whole rose
integrated the two velocity components separately and added the results instead of integrating the speed
substituted the x-coordinate two straight into the parameter slot instead of solving for the t that reaches the point
added the two velocity components and reported the result as a speed, which came out negative

problems.desc: Open explanation: the student must distinguish the velocity vector, the speed, and the slope dy/dx for a parametric curve, explain why a speed can never be negative while a component of velocity can, and explain why integrating half r squared over a full turn overcounts the area of a three-petal rose. Read the reasoning by hand; any argument that names speed as the magnitude of the velocity vector and identifies the repeated sweep of the rose earns full credit.
